commits.message:
feat(email-parsing): landing database for parsed emails

Replaces JSONL-files-under-/hermes-runtime storage (drafts, claim-and-
verify state, field provenance, exact-content dedupe index, transport
idempotency keys, intake history) with a dedicated Postgres database
owned by Hermes -- separate from Jobfynder Core's database, matching
the "Hermes proposes, Core executes" boundary (docs/hermes-architecture-
frozen-v1.md section 2). This is the foundation for actually tracking
parsed emails (search/filter/report instead of grepping files on disk),
for a real review frontend, and for self-learning classification --
none of those are practical against files on disk.

New: app/runtime/db.py (connection pool + schema, psycopg[binary,pool]),
scripts/hermes-landing-db-import-jsonl.py (one-time, idempotent import
of pre-existing JSONL data -- does not delete or modify the original
files, so they remain a rollback path).

Every storage module keeps its exact existing function signatures
(create_draft_object, get_claim_by_token, record_field_provenance, etc)
-- this is a storage-layer swap, not an API change; nothing outside
these modules needed to change except two real bugs the swap surfaced:

  - app/claim/service.py: _save_claim's UPDATE was missing expires_at
    in its SET list (caught by hermes-850-claim-check's expiry test) --
    the old JSONL version wrote the whole object so this was invisible
    there.
  - app/channels/service.py + app/runtime/intake_log.py: the transport-
    idempotency check (_seen_duplicate_keys, load_idempotency_keys) was
    a load-once-at-startup in-memory set per process. hermes-api and
    hermes-graph-consumer are separate processes -- each held its own
    stale snapshot, invisible to the other, and duplicates seen after
    startup were never persisted back into that snapshot either.
    Replaced with record_idempotency_key_if_new(), a single
    INSERT ... ON CONFLICT against the shared database: correct across
    processes and atomic (no separate check-then-insert race window).

hermes-postgres added to docker-compose.yml as a proper managed service
(not shared with Core's database), both hermes-api and
hermes-graph-consumer now depend_on it (service_healthy) and get
DATABASE_URL. Schema init (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, idempotent) runs
from both hermes-api's FastAPI startup hook and the consumer script's
own main() -- the consumer is not a FastAPI process, so it cannot share
that hook, and either process may be the first to actually query the
database.

Verified: full 8-script regression suite + the retry/DLQ suite, run
clean against an isolated, disposable test Postgres (reset and
re-verified after fixing the two bugs above) -- never against
production. Import script separately verified against a read-only copy
of the real /hermes-runtime data (140 drafts, 9 provenance rows, 137
idempotency keys imported correctly, spot-checked against the source).
